predecessors.name: Roman Empire
predecessors.text: the eastern half of the empire: the praetorian prefecture of the East (Thrace, Asia, Pontus, Oriens, Egypt) and the prefecture of Illyricum (the dioceses of Dacia and Macedonia), Arcadius's share at…

successors.name: Byzantine Empire
successors.text: everything: the same state continues without a break

ledger.x: 395: Lazica, the empire's client kingdom on the Black Sea.
395: the Huns pour through the Caucasus.
395: Alaric's Goths rise and march on Greece.
395: Theodosius dies; Arcadius rules the East from Constantinople.
397: Alaric's Goths are out of Greece.
437: the West recognises Eastern Illyricum; Sirmium becomes the prefecture's seat.
447: after the Utus, a strip south of the Danube is left to the Huns.
451: the Danube frontier recovered while Attila is in Gaul.
455: the Danube bank re-established after the Huns' collapse.
469: Cherson and the southern Crimea are drawn Eastern from this year by Cliopatria, which hands the cells over when its Hunnic Empire shrinks to a residue.
473: the Ghassanid Arabs become Roman foederati.
476: Odoacer rules Italy as the Eastern emperor's client.
483: Theodoric's Ostrogoths are federates on the lower Danube.
502: Kavad takes the Armenian and Mesopotamian fortresses.
510: Cliopatria gives the Gepids the Danube bank below Singidunum.
534: Gelimer surrenders; the Vandal kingdom is annexed.
535: Sicily. 'Belisarius took the island quickly. The only determined resistance, at Palermo, fell by late December' 535. Cliopatria adds Sicily in its 536 shape.
540: Khosrow I breaks the Perpetual Peace and sacks Antioch.
548: John Troglita ends the Moorish revolt.

552: Spania. Athanagild asked Justinian for help 'in autumn of 551 or winter of 552'; 'The army was probably sent in 552 and landed in June or July', defeating Agila 'in August or September 552'; 'A second force landed at Cartagena in early March 555', Cliopatria's year. The province held 'the Baetica coast from…
552: Narses wins at Taginae; Italy recovered.
555: the Danube bank below Singidunum returns from the Gepids in Cliopatria's 555 shape.
561: the Avars reach the Danube mouth.
567: Sirmium returns as the Gepid kingdom falls.
571-591: the war of Justin II and Maurice with Persia.
582-626: the Avar and Slav wars for the Balkans.
591: Khosrow II pays for his throne.
591: the war ends with Khosrow II's restoration; 'Byzantine victory'.
592: Spania shrinks further in Cliopatria's 592 shape.
603: Agilulf takes the Po valley cities.
613: the Ghassanid lands overrun with Syria.
614: Salona destroyed; the Dalmatian hinterland passes to the Slavs.
617: Lazica and western Iberia under Persian control; recovered in Heraclius's Caucasian campaigns of 624-626.

619: Egypt. The Persian invasion began in 617 or 618; 'a man named Peter betrayed the city to the Persians in June 619' (Alexandria, per the Khuzistan Chronicle); 'By 621 the province was securely in Persian hands'; Shahrbaraz 'ruled Egypt from Alexandria for about ten years'. Cliopatria removes Egypt only in 623.

623: Rhodes. 'Rhodes and other eastern Aegean islands fall' (622/623). Cliopatria keeps Rhodes Roman; hatched until the peace of 628. Rhodes page (2026-10-19): 'In 622/3, during the climactic Byzantine-Sasanian War of 602-628, Rhodes was captured by the Sasanian navy.'
626: Lazica and western Iberia recovered in the Caucasian campaigns.
626: the Avar war for the Balkans ends with the failed siege.
628: Rhodes returned under the peace, which restored 'all lost territories'; no page dates the island's handover.
628: Khosrow II overthrown; Kavad II makes peace.
629: Syria, Palestine, Egypt, Mesopotamia and Armenia evacuated by the Persians.
629: the Ghassanid phylarchate restored with Syria.
630: the Balkan interior passes to the Slavs.
632: the dossier hands over; the state continues.

wars.name: Hunnic invasion of 395
wars.outcome: A raid through the Caucasus: the Huns 'overran Armenia, pillaged Cappadocia, entered parts of Syria, threatened Antioch, and passed through Euphratesia'; no land changed hands.

wars.name: Alaric's revolt in Greece and Illyricum
wars.outcome: Alaric sacked Athens (396), was driven into Epirus by Stilicho, made magister militum per Illyricum by the East (397), lost his province when it was transferred to the West (399) and invaded Italy in late 401/402.

wars.name: Uldin's invasion of Thrace
wars.outcome: In the summer of 408 the Huns 'entered the Balkans and Thrace' and 'captured Castra Martis in Dacia Ripensis'; Uldin 'was forced to re-cross the Danube by March 23, 409'.

wars.name: Roman-Sasanian War of 421-422
wars.outcome: 'ended in an indecisive stalemate'; peace in 422 'without changes to the status quo' as the Huns menaced Constantinople; a ban on new frontier fortifications (Roman-Persian Wars page).

wars.name: Roman-Sasanian War of 440
wars.outcome: 'Yazdegerd II raided Roman Armenia' in 440; the page states no outcome.

wars.name: Hunnic wars of Attila
wars.outcome: The Huns took Sirmium, Singidunum, Margus and Viminacium (441), Ratiaria and Naissus (443), won at the Utus and destroyed Marcianople and Serdica (447); the peace of 447/448 (or 449) cost 6,000 pounds of gold, 2,100 a year, and a strip 'five days' journey…

wars.name: Dengizich's war on the Danube
wars.outcome: Dengizich crossed the frozen Danube in 467; Leo I answered that 'he was ready to do everything if they came to him and offered him obedience'; 'the war dragged on for two years'; Dinzirichus 'was killed by Anagastes, general in Thrace' in 469 and the Hun…

wars.name: Vandal expedition of 468
wars.outcome: 'the most ambitious campaign ever launched against the Vandal state': at Cape Bon 'the Vandals destroyed the Western fleet and part of the Eastern fleet using fire ships'.

wars.name: Anastasian War
wars.outcome: 'Inconclusive', 'Status quo ante bellum': Theodosiopolis, Martyropolis and Amida fell in 502-503, Amida was retaken in 504, the treaty of November 506 set a seven-year peace; Anastasius built Dara (505-507/508).

wars.name: Iberian War
wars.outcome: 'Inconclusive', ended by the Perpetual Peace of September 532: 'all territories seized during the war by either side were returned', 11,000 pounds of gold paid, 'Sasanians retained Iberia; Byzantines retained Lazica', the dux moved from Dara to Constantia.

wars.name: Vandalic War
wars.outcome: 'Decisive Byzantine victory'; 'Byzantine annexation of Vandal territory; establishment of Byzantine North Africa' (June 533 - March 534): Ad Decimum, Carthage (15 September 533), Tricamarum (December), Gelimer's surrender (March 534), the prefecture of Africa…

wars.name: Moorish wars in Africa
wars.outcome: Solomon's victories (535, 539), the mutiny of 536, Solomon killed at Cillium (544), Areobindus murdered (546); John Troglita 'defeated the Moors at the Fields of Cato' in early 548, 'ending the revolt that had lasted almost 15 years'.

wars.name: Gothic War (535-554)
wars.outcome: 'Byzantine victory', a 'pyrrhic victory': 'Sicily, the Italian Peninsula, and Dalmatia were conquered by the Byzantine Empire'; the Pragmatic Sanction (554); the last Gothic cities fell in 562; the Lombards came in 568.

wars.name: Khosrow I's invasion of Syria
wars.outcome: Khosrow 'invaded Syria, destroyed Antioch' and 'withdrew after extorting money'; the Roman invasion of Persian Armenia was ambushed at Anglon (543); a five-year truce in 545.

wars.name: Lazic War
wars.outcome: 'Disputed' result, 'Status quo ante bellum': Lazica defected to Persia (541), Petra fell to Bessas (551), Archaeopolis was retaken (556); the Fifty-Year Peace of 562 had Persia 'evacuate Lazica' for 30,000 nomismata a year and recognise it 'as a Roman vassal…

wars.name: Frankish-Alemannic invasion of Italy
wars.outcome: Narses 'destroyed the invaders at the Battle of the Volturnus' (554); no land changed hands.

wars.name: Byzantine Spania and the Visigothic reconquest
wars.outcome: The province won in 552-555 for Athanagild was taken back piece by piece: Asidona and Cordoba (Leovigild, 572), the inland to the Sierra Nevada (by 600), Malaga (Sisebut, 614-615), Cartagena and the last towns (Suinthila, 624); the Balearics stayed imperial.

wars.name: Lombard invasion of Italy
wars.outcome: Alboin crossed in spring 568; Milan fell in 569, Pavia in 572; the duchies of Spoleto and Benevento were founded (571-577); Agilulf took Parma, Piacenza, Padua, Cremona and Mantua by 603.

wars.name: Garmul's war on the Eastern Romans
wars.outcome: Garmul's forces killed the praetorian prefect Theodore and the magister militum Theoctistus in 570 and the magister militum Amabilis in 571 'although he failed to take any significant town'; the campaign 'launched in 577-78 AD, was brief and effective' and…

wars.name: Byzantine-Sasanian War of 572-591
wars.outcome: 'Byzantine victory': after the civil war of 589-591 'Khosrow II gives the Byzantine Empire most of Persian Armenia and western half of Iberia' and returned Dara and Martyropolis.

wars.name: Avar-Byzantine wars
wars.outcome: Infobox 'Byzantine victory' at the siege of Constantinople (29 June - 7/8 August 626), after which 'the Avars declined'; but 'much of the Balkans' was disputed and 'Byzantine authority collaps[ed] in the peninsula's interior', which the Slavs settled…

wars.name: Byzantine-Sasanian War of 602-628
wars.outcome: 'Byzantine victory', 'Status quo ante bellum': Nineveh (12 December 627), Dastagird plundered, Khosrow II overthrown (February 628); Kavad II returned 'all lost territories', an indemnity and the True Cross; Shahrbaraz's army left Egypt and Syria in summer…

wars.name: Battle of Mu'tah
wars.outcome: 'the first conflict between the Byzantines and the Arabs' (September 629), a Byzantine victory; in 630 'the Arabs launched an offensive into the Arabah and took al-Karak'.

certainty.note: The Persian frontier is sharp: the Armenian partition of 384/387 and the Mesopotamian fortress line (Nisibis Persian, Amida and, from 505, Dara Roman), confirmed by the treaties of 422 and 506.

The Perpetual Peace (September 532) fixes the eastern line sharply ('all territories seized ... were returned') until Khosrow's 540 raid; the Lazic front (541-562), the Gothic War's front in Italy and the Moorish interior of Africa (to…
Sharp in the east: the Fifty-Year Peace of 562 and the 591 settlement name the ceded cities (Dara, Martyropolis, Yerevan, Ani, Kars, Mtskheta).

Every frontier moves: the Persian conquests and their return (629) are drawn by province; the Balkan interior is Slavic settlement without a line (grey from 630); the 628 peace restores the 591 line in the east, sharp again from 629.
